idea: Singapore ERP: charge per gantry crossing is adjusted (up to 6 times a year) so road-section speeds stay inside a target band; higher charge when speeds are low, vehicle-type and time differentiated; Stockholm time-banded 10-20 SEK with daily cap 60 SEK; Milan emission-class toll. Model as a cordon of roads with a toll that shifts a share of trips to other mode/time/route.
does: Scenario tool: place a toll on a set of roads or a cordon, adjust it by rule (speed target band) between experiment runs, and compare KPIs and revenue vs no toll.
inputs: road set or cordon, charge by hour and vehicle type, target speed band, demand elasticity or mode-split utility term
outputs: charge schedule, cordon crossings, speeds, revenue, paired-t comparison vs baseline
existing: none (mode split by logit exists in institution_mode_split; no cost term)
notes: No formula in the book, only the feedback rule; elasticity must be assumed and labelled as such.

topic: Eco-speed harmonisation (variable speed limits) and fuel/emission KPI
idea: AERIS eco-lanes: variable speed limits that smooth stop-start gave up to 12% energy saving but 8% mobility loss; after tuning to keep mobility, about 5%. Eco-CACC 15-30%. ACMS has no fuel or emission KPI at all.
does: Add a fuel/CO2 proxy KPI (from speed and acceleration traces per vehicle) and let the assistant test a variable speed limit zone, reporting the energy vs mobility trade-off as the book frames it.
inputs: vehicle speed/accel samples, speed-limit zone, trigger rule
outputs: fuel/CO2 proxy per km, mean speed, travel time, trade-off table
notes: Book gives only outcomes, no emission formula; a published model (e.g. VT-micro or SUMO HBEFA-like polynomial) would need citing.

idea: Zurich: give transit only the least green time needed so other traffic is not disturbed; TSP considers schedule lateness and passengers on board in granting priority; priority is distinct from pre-emption (emergency only).
does: Report for each TSP grant the extra delay imposed on cross traffic and the bus saving, so agents can be scored on net person-delay and prompted to grant priority only when lateness or load justifies it.
inputs: TSP decisions log, per-approach delay, bus lateness and occupancy
outputs: net person-delay per decision, grant efficiency
existing: partial: TSP agent and Batch Run compare agents
notes: Conceptual; ACMS TSP likely already measures delay.
